title: Building predictive signaling models by perturbing yeast cells with time-varying stimulations resulting in distinct signaling responses
protocol: Implement time-varying cell culture environments in the laboratory as described in Ref (Thiemicke et al., 2019).
Treat cell cultures with stimulant concentrations that change over time.
Follow cell cultures treated with time-varying stimulations over time in a microfluidic flow chamber on a fluorescent microscope.
Collect measured bright field and fluorescent images of yeast cells showing nuclear localization of YFP-tagged Hog1 MAPK.
Use image processing codes for cell segmentation and quantification as reported in Refs (Johnson et al., 2021; Kesler et al., 2019).
Measure signaling activation time-traces using immunoblotting or fluorescent flow cytometry to parametrize underlying signaling models.
Generate the pump profile.
Download the codes to generate pump profiles.
Follow steps 1 to 5 in README.txt using MATLAB codes and excel files.
Set up and generate desired pump profiles.
Load generated pump profiles onto the syringe pump.
Prepare the flow setup for experimentation.
Prepare the microfluidic flow chamber on a microscope according to specified guidelines.
Add concentrated stimulus gradually to a mixing beaker with constant stirring.
Deliver time-varying stimulus from the mixing beaker to cells through tubing at a low constant rate.
Use a 3-way valve to switch between normal media and temporal gradient exposure for cells.
Compile the pathway as a dynamic ordinary differential equation (ODE) system using the appropriate MM function based on the matrices from steps B and C.
Arrange the vector of parameters Λ such that odd entries correspond to catalytic rate constants and even entries to Michaelis-Menten constants.
Use a customized Genetic Algorithm (GA) and MATLAB's fminsearch function for optimization.
Define the objective function as the sum of squared residuals between model predictions and data over all training datasets time-traces.
Minimize the objective function to find the set of best parameters Λ∗ that maximizes the likelihood of observing the training data.
Assemble the flow chambers.
Cut off all access glue and tubing on the bottom of the acryl slide with a razor blade.
Glue one side of the double sticky T-shaped spacer on the Pyrex slide with the tubing.
Move a plastic pen over the T-shaped spacer to remove air bubbles.
Remove the second sticky tape cover.
Place the ConA coated coverslip onto the fluidic channel so that the ConA stripe matches with the T-shaped space.
Use a plastic pen again to remove any remaining bubbles.
Measure the OD of the cells in the morning before the experiment to be OD = 0.5 at 600 nm.
Transfer 1.5 mL of cells (OD600–0.5) into each of three 1.5 mL centrifugation tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes for 5 min at 500G (rcf).
Remove access liquid until ∼100 μL are left in each tube.
Centrifuge the tubes on the bench-top centrifuge for 10 s.
Remove supernatant (∼60 μL).
Resuspend and combine the remaining 40 μL pellets from all three tubes into one.
Load cells to the flow chamber using a pipette and 100 μL tips.
Hookup the chamber onto the microscope after loading the cells.
Wait 5 min to allow the cells to stick to the ConA coverslip.
Image acquisition with time-lapse microscopy.
By moving in the xy-plane, select a field of view with optimal density of cells in a single z-plane.
Adjust the z-focus to see the boundary of the majority of cells as a white ring.
Record time-lapse images with both bright field (e.g., every 10 s) and fluorescent (e.g., every minute) channels.
Connect the flow chamber inlet with the 3-way valve (to media and mixing beaker) and its outlet to the pump2 in the flow setup according to the step 2(a).
Switch the inlet valve to the media (0 M).
Set the flow rate on the outlet syringe pump to 9 mL/min.
Turn on the pump and wash off any unbound cells with osmolyte-free media until all unbound cells are gone (∼1 min).
Reduce the outlet pump flow rate to 0.1 mL/min.
After the flow is stabilized, turn off the pump.
Close the valve to the media without osmolyte.
Switch the inlet tubing to the mixing beaker containing osmolyte-containing media.
Start the data acquisition.
Turn on the pumps simultaneously.
Ensure there are at least 3 YFP images taken before cells experience osmotic stimuli.
Quantify single cell signaling activation.
Download MATLAB codes from Jashnsaz_STARProtocols_2021/Jashnsaz_et_al_dir01_Models.
Generate models using downloaded MATLAB codes.
Use visualize_models.m to import Models.mat generated by running get_models.m.
Visualize network diagrams for all models using network_plot.m.
Reduce model complexity by grouping proteins together as nodes.
Consider a 4-node network topology for the signal transduction networks.
Simplify signal transduction networks into a general 4-node topology.
Model recurrent core network topologies capable of robust biological functions.
Group multiple proteins involved in signaling networks into virtual nodes.
Describe pathway activation dynamics and cellular responses accurately.
Account for branched signaling pathways converging at common downstream components.
Divide the timepoints of data into two sets.
Use a portion of the timepoints (25% selected randomly) for the first Genetic Algorithm and fminsearch call.
Use all timepoints of the training data for the second Genetic Algorithm and subsequent fminsearch call.
Define the objective function as one half of the sum of squared residuals of the model fit to the data.
Sample uniformly 200 parameter sets in [−3,+3] on a logarithmic scale base 10.
Return one parameter set after sampling and feed it into fminsearch.
Repeat uniform sampling every 4th iteration for larger parameter space exploration.
Adjust iteration interval if necessary.
Minimize the objective function with fminsearch using GA outputted parameter sets.
Collect best parameter sets after each second fminsearch iteration.
Resample 200 new parameter sets within [−0.5,+0.5] range from collected sets.
Sample new parameter sets for finer spacing of 0.005.
Run the GA for 20 generations, passing on one set with minimum objective value.
Implement a mutation function using best parameter sets from previous generation parents.
Parametrize the HOG model with experimentally measured Hog1 nuclear localization data.
Predict Hog1 signaling dynamics using parameter sets inferred from multiple independent training processes.
Evaluate the model’s ability to predict held out experimental Hog1 dynamics for each condition.
Define the parameter set resulting in the smallest prediction errors as the “true parameter set”.
Simulate synthetic signaling data using the true parameter set and 4-node model upon diverse cell stimulation conditions.
Generate diverse cell stimulation inputs changing according to step, linear, or quadratic functions over time.
Simulate signaling data from the true model under different time-varying stimulation inputs.
Simulate signaling data.
Solve the "true model" for the activation of the terminal kinase protein upon numerous cell stimulation input conditions.
Use polynomial functions to represent different temporal profiles of cell stimulations.
Generate signaling data over a wide range of cell stimulation conditions.
Capture cell-to-cell variability and measurement noise by generating single-cell trajectories.
Add experimentally realistic Gaussian white noise to model ODE solutions.
Calculate mean and standard deviation from single-cell trajectories over time as signaling activation data for each condition.
Simulate 30 independent synthetic datasets for each condition under independent single-cell noise.
Refer to these simulations as 30 "synthetic replicates" of the same data.
Train the true model with independent sets of simulated data generated using the true model.
Add Gaussian distributed noise to the simulated data to mimic experimentally realistic conditions.
Quantify fit errors for each condition.
Determine best parameter sets from the quantified data.
Evaluate uncertainty in the model parameters.
Validate model by predicting signaling responses for new conditions.
Predict the system’s behavior upon new conditions.
Generate numerous signaling data sets using simulated data.
Use a portion of the generated data sets to train the model.
Fit the model with six step training datasets.
Predict the signaling dynamics upon new cell stimulation conditions.
